title: People capture what we could not: the Captured filter and the home page list
description:
Ryan 2026-11-03. A continuous need from humans: accepted References whose contents could not be collected automatically, for example behind an I'm-not-a-robot gate. It is worth human effort to collect the highest-rated ones, by uploading a PDF, or select-all and paste. Organize the UI around this.

Filters: Reviewed (accepted or rejected, or not) replaces Unrated, All, Rated. New Captured filter (fully captured or not). A Reference the check doubts counts as not captured.

Newsroom home page: shows a few accepted, not-captured References. Highest-rated first, then most recent.

Design: a captureState field on Reference (full, thin, none, running; empty means none, because a monitor-discovered Reference has only its address), written with each capture change and by the backfill. Filtering reads existing indexes and drops rows client-side, so no new index and no sort restriction. An editor's complete verdict counts as full. No capture classifier exists yet: docs/reference-curation-pipeline.md records signals and editor labels for a future Cyclotron one, so today's check is the rule in lib/reference-capture.ts. Building that classifier is a follow-up. Every behaviour change ships with Gherkin; the epic ends with a p.apyr.us docs task.
